info.title: OpenVibe.Search API
info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Search as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.262.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

delete.summary: Index, replace or tombstone the calling service's own documents (search.index-document@1) and read its own inventory for reconciliation.
delete.description: **search.document.write** (first-party): Index, replace or tombstone the calling service's own documents (search.index-document@1) and read its own inventory for reconciliation. The owner in the path must be the principal's service slug (svc:wiki writes owner wiki only). Revision-ordered: an older revision never overwrites a newer one, and at equal revision a deletion wins.

get.summary: Query the index on behalf of a person: X-OV-Subject (usr_/gst_) plus the X-OV-Groups and X-OV-Entitlements the calling first-party service has just resolved for that person.
get.description:
**search.query.delegate** (first-party): Query the index on behalf of a person: X-OV-Subject (usr_/gst_) plus the X-OV-Groups and X-OV-Entitlements the calling first-party service has just resolved for that person. Without X-OV-Subject the service sees public documents only. Drafts, unpublished and deleted documents are never returned to anyone.

**search.query.run** (public): Query the network index as anyone (roadmap §30.2 search.query, search.suggest, search.facets.read): anonymous callers get public, published documents only, and a signed-in person's Network token adds the documents whose access list names them or their role. Covers title suggestions, facet counts (facets=, facet.<key>=) and reading one document; a document the caller may not see is the same 404 as a missing one. Served publicly at search.openvibe.network. A first-party service asking for a person uses search.query.delegate (today Search requires that id for any service token).

get.summary: One search over several scopes (plan 2026-10-28 §4.5, the Search Fabric): network (Search's index, permission-aware as search.query.run), mine (the person's own private documents), web (OpenVibe's ope
get.description: **search.fabric.query** (public): One search over several scopes (plan 2026-10-28 §4.5, the Search Fabric): network (Search's index, permission-aware as search.query.run), mine (the person's own private documents), web (OpenVibe's open index, then paid providers in a ladder, cached), with route.explain saying what answered and what it cost. Anonymous callers get network results and web results from the open index and the cache; a signed-in person or a first-party service (X-OV-Subject for mine) also reaches paid providers within OpenVibe's daily caps. Providers never receive an account identifier. The same operation is the SDK's createSearchClient().query() and the MCP tool openvibe.search.

common.no-body.v1.title: NoBody
common.no-body.v1.description: common.no-body@1: the capability's request carries no body; its parameters are the path and query of the routes in implementedBy (an id, a page cursor). An input schema that says so explicitly, so every active capability names one (roadmap WS-C task 4).

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

search.document-write-request.v1.title: SearchDocumentWriteRequest
search.document-write-request.v1.description: search.document-write-request@1: the request of search.document.write on OpenVibe.Search (a service writes and reads only the documents it owns). PUT /api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id: a search.index-document@1 (owner, type and id come from the path; a body that names others is 422). DELETE /api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id?revision= (a tombstone) and the owner reads (GET /api/v1/owners/:owner/documents, …/documents/:type/:id, …/rejections) take no body.

search.fabric-request.v1.title: SearchFabricRequest
search.fabric-request.v1.description: search.fabric-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/query (or the query string of GET /api/v1/query, scopes comma-separated), capability search.fabric.query. One search over several scopes, routed the cheapest way that answers (plan 2026-10-28 §4.5). network: Search's own index, permission-aware exactly as search.query.run; mine: the caller's own private documents (a signed-in person, or a service with X-OV-Subject); web: OpenVibe's open index first, then paid providers in a ladder, each result keeping its provider, date and URL. Providers never receive an account identifier. A scope the caller may not use (mine without a person; web's paid providers for an anonymous caller, who gets cached and open-index results only) is reported in route.explain, never an error. The other scopes are facets of the same indexes and are accepted for forward compatibility; v1 answers them as network results filtered by kind.

scopes.description: Where to look; results are grouped by scope. Default: network.

filters.description: Narrow the network and mine scopes (never widen what the caller may see).

site.description: web: results from this host only.

freshness.description: How recent results must be, where the source dates them.

depth.description: quick: indexes and caches only (no paid provider); standard: the ladder until a step answers; deep: every step, merged.

answer.description: Ask for a short cited answer written by AI from the results. Never without citations; labelled AI. A deployment may decline (answer: null, with the reason in route.explain).

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous page (network and mine only).

search.fabric-result.v1.title: SearchFabricResult
search.fabric-result.v1.description: search.fabric-result@1: the answer of search.fabric.query. results come grouped by scope order (the room's own first when the caller asked for it); every web result keeps its provider, URL and date; route.explain says, step by step, what was asked, what answered, from cache or not, and what it cost. The query is never echoed: a page renders results without writing the query into its HTML (the ?q= rule).

kind.description: document: in Search's index (owner, type, id set); page: a web page (provider set).

retrieved_at.description: When a web page was read (by the provider or the open index).

provider.description: page: who found it (open_index, deepseek, wikipedia, brave, …).

score.description: Rank within its scope (higher first); not comparable across scopes.

ranks.description: 1-based position in the keyword and vector top-100 lists; null when absent from that list.

groups.description: How many results each scope gave on this page.

label.const: Written by AI from these sources

skipped.description: Why the step did not run (not allowed for this caller, quick depth, an earlier step answered, provider standing down).

cost_usd.description: What this query cost OpenVibe (paid provider calls; cached answers cost 0).

search.index-document.v1.title: IndexDocument
search.index-document.v1.description: What an owning service tells OpenVibe.Search about one of its resources (roadmap §15.12, §4.2 A). The owner stays the source of truth; Search keeps a revision-ordered, permission-aware copy for discovery. A document with deleted=true is a tombstone: it removes the resource from every result and wins over any upsert with the same or an older revision.

owner.description: Owning service id (wiki, blog, news, community, sources…). Only that service may write the document.

type.description: Resource type inside the owner (page, post, story, entity, offer, coupon, instrument, item…).

id.description: Resource id inside owner+type. Stable across revisions.

revision.description: Owner's monotonic revision of the resource. An older revision never overwrites a newer one; at equal revision a deletion wins.

deleted.description: Deletion marker. true = tombstone; every other content field is ignored.

visibility.description: public: anyone. unlisted: never listed except to ACL matches; fetchable by exact id by a signed-in subject. members: subjects, groups or entitlements in acl. private: subjects in acl.subjects only. draft: never served.

acl.description: Who may see a non-public document. Ignored for public documents. Empty means nobody (for members/private) or direct-id only (for unlisted).

groups.description: Opaque group keys owned by some service, e.g. role:admin (Network role), wiki.space:spc_…:member.

entitlements.description: Entitlement keys (VIP/Billing), e.g. vip.plan:pln_…. Only a first-party service that just resolved them may present them for a viewer.

body.description: Plain text for full-text search (no HTML). Keep it under the Events payload limit when publishing through Events.

facets.description: Filterable values (category, tags, space, author subject, currency…). Filter with facet.<key>=<value>.

provenance.description: Where the content came from: typed references to source records (Sources items, citations, Media objects).

stub.description: true when the reference came from a stub provider; the document is then never indexable.

publication_state.description: Only published documents are ever served.

indexability.description: The owner's deterministic indexability decision (publishing packages, roadmap §32.3). Search can only make it stricter.

reasons.description: Known reasons: draft, private, members_only, unlisted, not_published, deleted, thin_content, duplicate_without_canonical, unsupported_claims, unsourced, stub_provider, sensitive_unreviewed, ai_unreviewed, missing_canonical_url, third_party_content, owner_decision.

search.owner-result.v1.title: SearchOwnerResult
search.owner-result.v1.description: search.owner-result@1: answers of search.document.write on OpenVibe.Search. PUT and DELETE /api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id → search.write-result@1 (stale and conflicting revisions are 409 problems); GET /api/v1/owners/:owner/documents?type=&after=&limit= → { owner, documents, next_after } (reconciliation: type, id, revision, deleted, exposure, hash, indexed_at); GET /api/v1/owners/:owner/documents/:type/:id → { document, effective_indexability, exposure, via, event_id, indexed_at } (the stored document); GET /api/v1/owners/:owner/rejections?after= → { rejections, next_after } (index-document events Search refused, at most 200).

search.query-result.v1.title: SearchQueryResult
search.query-result.v1.description: search.query-result@1: the answer of GET /api/v1/search — one page of hits the caller may see, a cursor for the next page, and facet counts when asked. Never a total count and never an ACL.

indexable.description: false for a noindex document the caller may still see.

snippet_html.description: Escaped text with <mark> around the matches; nothing else.

ranks.description: 1-based position in the keyword and vector top-100 lists; null when absent from that list.

explain.description: How this page was ranked; reason is present only when ranking is keyword.

search.query.v1.title: SearchQuery
search.query.v1.description: search.query@1: the query string of GET /api/v1/search (and, with q/owner/type/limit only, GET /api/v1/suggest), capabilities search.query.run and search.query.delegate. Who sees what is decided by Search per hit: anonymous callers get public, published, indexable documents; a person also restricted documents naming them; a delegating service passes X-OV-Subject. Filters narrow; they never widen visibility.

q.description: Words to match (FTS5; empty lists by recency).

type.description: One document type within the owner (channel, vod, thread, …).

facets.description: Comma-separated facet keys to count over what the caller can see.

^facet\\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$.description: A facet filter (facet.<key>=<value>); repeat the parameter for several values.

search.read-result.v1.title: SearchReadResult
search.read-result.v1.description: search.read-result@1: answers of search.query.run and search.query.delegate on OpenVibe.Search. GET /api/v1/search → search.query-result@1; GET /api/v1/suggest?q=&owner=&type=&limit= → { suggestions } (title prefixes, at most 20, only documents the caller may see); GET /api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id → { document } (one document by exact id, if the caller may see it; 404 otherwise).

search.write-result.v1.title: SearchWriteResult
search.write-result.v1.description: search.write-result@1: the answer of PUT /api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id (search.document.write). applied: stored (or a tombstone recorded); unchanged: the same revision with the same content. A revision older than the stored one is a 409 problem search.stale_revision; the same revision with different content is 409 search.revision_conflict.

stored_revision.description: What Search held before this write (null: nothing).

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
